Goal: Add /api/telemetry/install + app_installs, and a Session Manager panel on /api/admin/observability

## Where this comes from

Claude Code Session Manager (the Electron desktop app published to npm as `claude-code-session-manager`, source at `~/Projects/session-manager`) is adding "phone home" telemetry so its author can see who is running it and collect the errors real users hit. We surveyed bilko.run as the collection platform and found that **you already have almost everything we need** — so this is a small extension request, not a new subsystem.

Session Manager will start sending to your existing, already-deployed routes in `server/routes/telemetry.ts`:

- `POST /api/telemetry/event` → `funnel_events`, with `app: "session-manager"`
- `POST /api/telemetry/log` → `app_logs`
- `POST /api/telemetry/error` → `app_errors`

It conforms to your existing contract exactly (`{ batch: [...] }`, ≤ 50 records, your field names, your clamps). **No change is needed on your side for those three signals.** Session Manager's `visitor_id` will be a stable anonymous install UUID persisted at `~/.config/session-manager/telemetry.json` on the user's machine; `session_id` is a per-process run id. No prompts, transcripts, file paths, project names or emails are sent.

## What we are asking for

### 1. A durable install record — `POST /api/telemetry/install` + an `app_installs` table

The one thing your schema cannot express today is **"once per machine"** identity. A desktop app's install profile is a slowly-changing dimension, not an event: the interesting query is "how many distinct installs ran version 0.81.0 this week, on which OS/arch, and how many are new" — and answering that from `funnel_events` means de-duplicating an append-only stream on every read.

Suggested shape (upsert-by-install-id, mirroring how `usage_daily` is keyed rather than logged):

```
CREATE TABLE app_installs (
  install_id     TEXT PRIMARY KEY,   -- client-minted UUID, the anonymous identity
  app            TEXT NOT NULL,      -- 'session-manager'
  app_version    TEXT,
  platform       TEXT,               -- 'linux' | 'darwin'
  os_release     TEXT,
  arch           TEXT,
  cpu_count      INTEGER,
  total_mem_mb   INTEGER,
  node_version   TEXT,
  electron_version TEXT,
  install_channel TEXT,              -- 'npx' | 'dev' | 'unknown'
  locale         TEXT,
  timezone       TEXT,
  identify_email TEXT,               -- optional, user-supplied opt-in only; usually NULL
  first_seen_at  INTEGER NOT NULL,
  last_seen_at   INTEGER NOT NULL,
  seen_count     INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 1
);
CREATE INDEX idx_app_installs_app_last_seen ON app_installs (app, last_seen_at DESC);
```

`POST /api/telemetry/install` should: upsert on `install_id`, preserve `first_seen_at`, bump `last_seen_at` and `seen_count`, and overwrite the profile fields (so a version upgrade or an OS upgrade is reflected). Please reuse the conventions already in `server/routes/telemetry.ts` rather than inventing new ones — the same per-IP `bumpAndCheck` dual-window rate limiter (a low limit like 60/min is plenty; a well-behaved client posts this at most once per app-version), the same `clamp()` on every string field, unauthenticated like its three siblings, and returning `{ ok: true }`.

Until this exists, Session Manager sends the machine profile as an `install.machine` event on `/api/telemetry/event`, so nothing is blocked — but that stream is not queryable as "distinct installs" and we would rather not build a de-dup view on top of it.

### 2. A Session Manager panel on `/api/admin/observability`

`server/routes/admin-observability.ts` already rolls up `app_errors` by app and `app_logs` by app+level, which will pick up `session-manager` rows for free. What is missing for this use case:

- installs: total, active in the last 7/30 days, new in the last 7 days, and a breakdown by `platform` / `arch` / `app_version`
- **errors grouped by version** — the highest-value query for a desktop app, because it answers "did the release I just shipped make things worse", which the current group-by-app rollup cannot
- top error signatures for `session-manager` by count (you already do a `msg` sample per app; a top-N with counts would be more useful)

### 3. Retention

`app_errors` / `app_logs` have no stated retention policy that we could find. Desktop crash reports arrive in bursts (one OOM-killed machine can produce a lot of correlated rows), so a cap or a scheduled prune would be worth deciding on deliberately before this traffic starts rather than after.

## Notes / non-asks

- **Do not change or rename the three existing telemetry routes or their field names.** Session Manager is building against them as-is, and has a contract test that replays your exact `INSERT` column order. If you need to change them, that test will need to change in lockstep — please send feedback back the other way first.
- Nothing here needs auth added. These are anonymous ingest endpoints by design, consistent with the three that already exist.
- This does not touch the `sm-relay` routes or the web-remote relay; that stays exactly as it is.

## Reference

- Your side: `server/routes/telemetry.ts`, `server/routes/admin-observability.ts`, `server/db.ts`, `data/contentgrade.db`
- Our side (for the payload shapes): the queued PRD chain `1139`–`1143` under `~/Projects/session-manager/session-manager-operations/scheduler/epics/bug-collection-i-want-to-enhance-the-session-man-ad557134/prds/`

Feedback delivered to /home/bilko/Projects/session-manager as a proposed session (bilko-run-api-telemetry-install-is-live-here-is--7c619698): "bilko.run: /api/telemetry/install is live — here is the exact contract". It will not run until a human in that project approves it.

**Report verified against the code, and implemented.** Commit `ee2b5ea`, pushed to `origin/main`.

The claim held exactly: `server/routes/telemetry.ts` has the three routes with the described shape, `app_logs`/`app_errors` exist in `server/db.ts` with no install identity and no retention, and `admin-observability.ts` rolls up by app only.

**1. `POST /api/telemetry/install` + `app_installs`** (`server/routes/telemetry.ts:…`, `server/db.ts`)
Table is exactly the proposed shape plus the index. Route is unauthenticated, uses the same `bumpAndCheck` limiter (60/min) and same `clamp()`. Upsert preserves `first_seen_at`, bumps `last_seen_at`/`seen_count`, overwrites the profile.

Two deliberate deviations, both communicated back:
- **Not batched** — takes a flat object, not `{ batch: [...] }`. A once-per-process upsert doesn't need the envelope. Missing `install_id` → `400 install_id_required`.
- **`identify_email` is `COALESCE`d**, so a later post without it doesn't wipe an opted-in address.

**2. Panel** — `GET /api/admin/observability/installs?app=&days=&limit=`: totals/active7/active30/new7, platform/arch/version breakdowns, `errorsByVersion` (count *and* distinct-machine count), top-N signatures with counts. Made a sub-route rather than a field on the main payload because `rows` there is keyed by published-app slug and a desktop app would be an all-null row; the main payload gains a `desktopApps` teaser so it's discoverable. Also added `idx_app_errors_app_version_created` so the version rollup doesn't table-scan.

**3. Retention** — `app_logs` 30d/200k rows, `app_errors` 90d/100k rows, whichever binds first, oldest-first. Pruned opportunistically on the ingest path (≤ once/10min per process, since nothing schedules in that process) and wrapped so a prune failure can never fail an ingest.

The three existing routes and their INSERT column order are untouched, so their contract test still passes. 319 tests pass, typecheck clean; 11 new tests across `tests/telemetry.tes…

Goal: Add /api/telemetry/install + app_installs, and a Session Manager panel on /api/admin/observability

## Where this comes from

Claude Code Session Manager (the Electron desktop app published to npm as `claude-code-session-manager`, source at `~/Projects/session-manager`) is adding "phone home" telemetry so its author can see who is running it and collect the errors real users hit. We surveyed bilko.run as the collection platform and found that **you already have almost everything we need** — so this is a small extension request, not a new subsystem.

Session Manager will start sending to your existing, already-deployed routes in `server/routes/telemetry.ts`:

- `POST /api/telemetry/event` → `funnel_events`, with `app: "session-manager"`
- `POST /api/telemetry/log` → `app_logs`
- `POST /api/telemetry/error` → `app_errors`

It conforms to your existing contract exactly (`{ batch: [...] }`, ≤ 50 records, your field names, your clamps). **No change is needed on your side for those three signals.** Session Manager's `visitor_id` will be a stable anonymous install UUID persisted at `~/.config/session-manager/telemetry.json` on the user's machine; `session_id` is a per-process run id. No prompts, transcripts, file paths, project names or emails are sent.

## What we are asking for

### 1. A durable install record — `POST /api/telemetry/install` + an `app_installs` table

The one thing your schema cannot express today is **"once per machine"** identity. A desktop app's install profile is a slowly-changing dimension, not an event: the interesting query is "how many distinct installs ran version 0.81.0 this week, on which OS/arch, and how many are new" — and answering that from `funnel_events` means de-duplicating an append-only stream on every read.

Suggested shape (upsert-by-install-id, mirroring how `usage_daily` is keyed rather than logged):

```
CREATE TABLE app_installs (
  install_id     TEXT PRIMARY KEY,   -- client-minted UUID, the anonymous identity
  app            TEXT NOT NULL,      -- 'session-manager'
  app_version    TEXT,
  platform       TEXT,               -- 'linux' | 'darwin'
  os_release     TEXT,
  arch           TEXT,
  cpu_count      INTEGER,
  total_mem_mb   INTEGER,
  node_version   TEXT,
  electron_version TEXT,
  install_channel TEXT,              -- 'npx' | 'dev' | 'unknown'
  locale         TEXT,
  timezone       TEXT,
  identify_email TEXT,               -- optional, user-supplied opt-in only; usually NULL
  first_seen_at  INTEGER NOT NULL,
  last_seen_at   INTEGER NOT NULL,
  seen_count     INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 1
);
CREATE INDEX idx_app_installs_app_last_seen ON app_installs (app, last_seen_at DESC);
```

`POST /api/telemetry/install` should: upsert on `install_id`, preserve `first_seen_at`, bump `last_seen_at` and `seen_count`, and overwrite the profile fields (so a version upgrade or an OS upgrade is reflected). Please reuse the conventions already in `server/routes/telemetry.ts` rather than inventing new ones — the same per-IP `bumpAndCheck` dual-window rate limiter (a low limit like 60/min is plenty; a well-behaved client posts this at most once per app-version), the same `clamp()` on every string field, unauthenticated like its three siblings, and returning `{ ok: true }`.

Until this exists, Session Manager sends the machine profile as an `install.machine` event on `/api/telemetry/event`, so nothing is blocked — but that stream is not queryable as "distinct installs" and we would rather not build a de-dup view on top of it.

### 2. A Session Manager panel on `/api/admin/observability`

`server/routes/admin-observability.ts` already rolls up `app_errors` by app and `app_logs` by app+level, which will pick up `session-manager` rows for free. What is missing for this use case:

- installs: total, active in the last 7/30 days, new in the last 7 days, and a breakdown by `platform` / `arch` / `app_version`
- **errors grouped by version** — the highest-value query for a desktop app, because it answers "did the release I just shipped make things worse", which the current group-by-app rollup cannot
- top error signatures for `session-manager` by count (you already do a `msg` sample per app; a top-N with counts would be more useful)

### 3. Retention

`app_errors` / `app_logs` have no stated retention policy that we could find. Desktop crash reports arrive in bursts (one OOM-killed machine can produce a lot of correlated rows), so a cap or a scheduled prune would be worth deciding on deliberately before this traffic starts rather than after.

Loaded by every agent persona in this repo. Rules here must hold regardless of whether the
agent is developing, trading, researching, or running ops. Anything role-specific belongs in
that role's persona file instead.

> **Origin note.** The three sections below were previously generated into `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md`
> by Claude Code's preset system as
> `<!-- claude-presets:start id=local-time,terse,socratic,correctness-over-quick-wins,do-both-dont-choose -->`.
> They are now owned here so they are versioned like everything else, and that block has been
> removed from the loader. **Do not re-enable those presets via `/config`** — doing so re-writes
> the block into `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md` and you get both copies. Edit this file instead.

## Time and timezone

- When stating any time, date, or deadline, use the user's local timezone: America/Los_Angeles (Pacific Time, PST/PDT depending on DST).
- Never use UTC, server time, or your own assumed timezone in user-facing replies. Convert if necessary.
- When showing a time, include the zone abbreviation (e.g., "3:15 PM PDT") so it is unambiguous.
- For relative phrasing ("tomorrow", "in 2 hours"), anchor to the user's local clock, not UTC.

## Communication style

- Be extremely concise. Lead with the answer or the diff.
- No preamble, no trailing summaries, no recap of what you just did.
- If the answer fits in one sentence, use one sentence. Skip pleasantries.

## Working style

- When a request has genuine ambiguity (scope, acceptance criteria, edge cases, framework choice), ask 3-5 focused clarifying questions before writing code.
- Don't ask for confirmation of the obvious — just for decisions that would cost real time to redo.
- When a choice is framed as "quick win vs. the longer correct way", always take the correct, more laborious path — do not ask.
- Don't offer a fast-but-partial path as an option; pick the thorough, correct solution by default.
- When the choice is "do A, do B, or do both", always do both A and B — do not ask which.
- Treat inclusive options as a signal to deliver the complete set, not to pick one.

## Automation model pinning

Any script or process that shells out to `claude --print` / `claude -p` **must** pin `--model`
explicitly.

Unpinned calls inherit whatever the CLI's current default model is, which drifts over time
(e.g. Opus → Fable) — silently and unboundedly multiplying the cost of batch/cron automation
that assumed a cheap model. This has bitten multiple projects, which is why it is a hard rule.

When writing *or reviewing* any `claude -p` call site — PRD executors, bots, classifiers, hooks
— check for an explicit `--model` flag before shipping it.

## Time and timezone

- When stating any time, date, or deadline, use the user's local timezone: America/Los_Angeles (Pacific Time, PST/PDT depending on DST).
- Never use UTC, server time, or your own assumed timezone in user-facing replies. Convert if necessary.

- For relative phrasing ("tomorrow", "in 2 hours"), anchor to the user's local clock, not UTC.

## Communication style

- Be extremely concise. Lead with the answer or the diff.
- No preamble, no trailing summaries, no recap of what you just did.
- If the answer fits in one sentence, use one sentence. Skip pleasantries.

## Working style

- When a request has genuine ambiguity (scope, acceptance criteria, edge cases, framework choice), ask 3-5 focused clarifying questions before writing code.
- Don't ask for confirmation of the obvious — just for decisions that would cost real time to redo.
- When a choice is framed as "quick win vs. the longer correct way", always take the correct, more laborious path — do not ask.

that assumed a cheap model. This has bitten multiple projects, which is why it is a hard rule.

## Projects hosting pattern

Three host kinds, declared in `src/data/projectsRegistry.ts`. Full spec in [`docs/host-contract.md`](docs/host-contract.md).

| Kind | Path | When to use |
|---|---|---|
| `react-route` | `/products/<slug>` | App needs shared auth/credits and is small enough to live in this bundle. Existing AI tools. |
| `static-path` | `/projects/<slug>/` | App is built in its own repo, dropped into `public/projects/<slug>/`. **Default for new apps.** |
| `external-url` | other domain | App lives elsewhere |

**URL canonicalization (enforced by `src/App.tsx`):**
- `/projects/<slug>` (no trailing slash, react-route) → redirects to `/products/<slug>`
- `/app/<old-slug>` → redirects to `/products/<canonical-slug>`
- `/projects/<slug>/` (trailing slash, static-path) → served by Fastify static, never hits the SPA

**Adding a new app from another Claude session:** read [`docs/host-contract.md`](docs/host-contract.md) and use the [`bilko-host` MCP](mcp-host-server/README.md). Don't edit `projectsRegistry.ts` by hand from a sibling repo.

The portfolio (`/`, `/products`, `⌘K`) reads from `projectsRegistry.ts`, so once registered the app shows up everywhere. Static-path and external apps trigger a full page load on click (so Fastify serves the static bundle); React routes use SPA navigation.

### Shared Component Kit (`src/components/tool-page/`)
- `ToolHero` — Dark hero section with title, tagline, optional tab toggle

- `useToolApi` — Auth, submit, compare, generate, error/loading/token state

### Backend Patterns (`server/`)
- `server/routes/tools/` — One file per AI tool. `_shared.ts` holds the rate limiter, IP hashing, usage tracking, and the inverse-mode generator helper. `index.ts` is the barrel that registers all tools. // Per-IP rate limiter (same dual-window pattern as analytics.ts).
const _counts = new Map<string, { count: number; windowStart: number }>();
const WINDOW_MS = 60_000;

function bumpAndCheck(key: string, limit: number): boolean {
  const now = Date.now();
  const e = _counts.get(key);
  if (!e || now - e.windowStart > WINDOW_MS) {
    _counts.set(key, { count: 1, windowStart: now });
    // Evict stale entries when map gets large.
    if (_counts.size > 5000) {
      for (const [k, v] of _counts) {
        if (now - v.windowStart > WINDOW_MS) _counts.delete(k);
      }
    }
    return true;
  }
  e.count += 1;
  return e.count <= limit;

function ipKey(req: { ip?: string; headers: Record<string, string | string[] | undefined> }): string {

function safeMeta(val: unknown, maxBytes: number): string {
  try { return JSON.stringify(val ?? {}).slice(0, maxBytes); } catch { return '{}'; }

import Fastify from 'fastify';
import { initDb, dbAll, dbRun } from '../server/db.js';
import { registerTelemetryRoutes } from '../server/routes/telemetry.js';

const app = Fastify({ trustProxy: true, logger: false });
registerTelemetryRoutes(app);

beforeAll(async () => {
  await initDb();
  await app.ready();
});

beforeEach(async () => {
  await dbRun('DELETE FROM app_logs');
  await dbRun('DELETE FROM app_errors');
});

function inject(method: 'POST', url: string, body: unknown, ip = '10.0.0.1') {
  return app.inject({
    method,
    url,
    headers: { 'content-type': 'application/json', 'x-forwarded-for': ip },
    body: JSON.stringify(body),
  });
}

describe('Telemetry ingest — /api/telemetry/log', () => {
  it('happy path: batch of 3 writes 3 rows', async () => {
    const res = await inject('POST', '/api/telemetry/log', {
      batch: [
        { app: 'test-app', version: '1.0.0', level: 'info', msg: 'hello', ts: Date.now() },
        { app: 'test-app', version: '1.0.0', level: 'warn', msg: 'careful', ts: Date.now() },
        { app: 'test-app', version: '1.0.0', level: 'error', msg: 'oops', ts: Date.now() },
      ],
    });
    expect(res.statusCode).toBe(200);
    const rows = await dbAll('SELECT * FROM app_logs WHERE app = ?', 'test-app');
    expect(rows).toHaveLength(3);
  });

  it('invalid level is silently skipped', async () => {
    const res = await inject('POST', '/api/telemetry/log', {
      batch: [
        { app: 'test-app', version: '1.0.0', level: 'pwn', msg: 'hax', ts: Date.now() },
        { app: 'test-app', version: '1.0.0', level: 'info', msg: 'legit', ts: Date.now() },
      ],
    }, '10.0.0.2');
    expect(res.statusCode).toBe(200);
    const rows = await dbAll('SELECT * FROM app_logs WHERE app = ?', 'test-app');
    expect(rows).toHaveLength(1); // only the valid row
    expect((rows[0] as Record<string, unknown>).level).toBe('info');
  });
});

// --- Retention -------------------------------------------------------------
// app_logs / app_errors are unbounded ingest tables with no external scheduler
// to sweep them, and desktop crash reports arrive in correlated bursts (one
// OOM-killed machine can emit thousands of rows in a minute). So the prune is
// opportunistic, on the same request path that writes: at most once every
// PRUNE_EVERY_MS per process, delete anything past the age cap, then trim the
// oldest rows back to the row cap. Cheap (two bounded DELETEs), and it cannot
// let a burst grow the table without bound the way a nightly job would.
const LOG_RETENTION_DAYS = 30;
const ERROR_RETENTION_DAYS = 90;
const MAX_LOG_ROWS = 200_000;
const MAX_ERROR_ROWS = 100_000;
const PRUNE_EVERY_MS = 10 * 60_000;

let _lastPruneAt = 0;

export async function pruneTelemetry(): Promise<void> {
  const now = Math.floor(Date.now() / 1000);
  await dbRun('DELETE FROM app_logs WHERE created_at < ?', now - LOG_RETENTION_DAYS * 86_400);
  await dbRun('DELETE FROM app_errors WHERE created_at < ?', now - ERROR_RETENTION_DAYS * 86_400);

  for (const [table, cap] of [['app_logs', MAX_LOG_ROWS], ['app_errors', MAX_ERROR_ROWS]] as const) {
    const row = await dbGet<{ n: number }>(`SELECT COUNT(*) AS n FROM ${table}`);
    const excess = (row?.n ?? 0) - cap;

        `DELETE FROM ${table} WHERE id IN (SELECT id FROM ${table} ORDER BY created_at ASC LIMIT ?)`,
        excess,
      );

  }
}

    expect(body.installs.byArch.find((a: any) => a.arch === 'arm64').n).toBe(1);
    expect(body.installs.byVersion.find((v: any) => v.app_version === '0.82.0').installs).toBe(1);
  });

All three asks are done. This message is the contract you should build against — the shipped route differs from your suggested shape in two small ways, noted below.

## 1. POST /api/telemetry/install — live

Unauthenticated, same as its three siblings. Same per-IP dual-window `bumpAndCheck` limiter, limit 60/min. Returns `{ ok: true }` on success.

IMPORTANT — this endpoint is NOT batched. It takes a single flat JSON object, not `{ batch: [...] }`. A one-per-process upsert did not justify the batch envelope. Post the profile object directly:

```json
{
  "install_id": "…uuid…",      // REQUIRED — 400 {"error":"install_id_required"} if missing/empty
  "app": "session-manager",
  "app_version": "0.81.0",
  "platform": "linux",
  "os_release": "6.18.7",
  "arch": "x64",
  "cpu_count": 16,
  "total_mem_mb": 32768,
  "node_version": "22.3.0",
  "electron_version": "31.0.0",
  "install_channel": "npx",
  "locale": "en-US",
  "timezone": "America/Los_Angeles",
  "identify_email": null
}
```

Field limits (strings are truncated, never rejected): install_id 80, app 60, app_version 20, platform 20, os_release 80, arch 20, node_version 20, electron_version 20, install_channel 20, locale 20, timezone 60, identify_email 160. `cpu_count` and `total_mem_mb` are coerced to a non-negative integer; a non-numeric value stores NULL rather than failing the request.

Semantics: upsert on `install_id`. `first_seen_at` preserved, `last_seen_at` set to now, `seen_count` incremented, every other profile field overwritten so a version or OS upgrade is reflected. One deliberate exception — an absent or null `identify_email` does NOT wipe a previously opted-in one (`COALESCE(excluded, existing)`). If you need to clear it, send an explicit empty value and tell us; today that is also treated as absent.

The table is `app_installs` with exactly the columns you proposed, plus `idx_app_installs_app_last_seen`. You can stop sending the `install.machine` event on `/api/telemetry/event` once you cut over — or keep both during a transition, they do not conflict.

## 2. Admin panel — live

`GET /api/admin/observability/installs?app=session-manager&days=30&limit=20` (admin-only). Returns install totals + active7/active30/new7, breakdowns by platform/arch/version, `errorsByVersion` (error count AND distinct machine count per version — 10 000 errors from one looping install reads very differently from 10 across 10 installs), top-N error signatures with counts and last-seen, and log level counts. It is a sub-route rather than a field on `/api/admin/observability` because that payload's `rows` are keyed by published static-app slug, and a desktop app has no manifest, synthetic run or egress — it would be an all-null row. The main payload does gain a `desktopApps` teaser (`[{app, installs, active7}]`) so the panel is discoverable.

`app` is a parameter, not a hardcode — any future phone-home client gets the same panel for free.

## 3. Retention — decided

`app_logs`: 30 days or 200 000 rows. `app_errors`: 90 days or 100 000 rows. Whichever binds first; the row cap trims oldest-first. Pruned opportunistically on the ingest path (at most once per 10 minutes per process) because there is no scheduler in that process, and wrapped so a retention failure can never fail an ingest. This means a correlated crash burst is bounded rather than unbounded — if Session Manager can ever emit more than ~100k errors in 90 days legitimately, tell us and we will raise the cap rather than let you silently lose the tail.

## Non-asks honored

The three existing routes, their field names and their INSERT column order are untouched — your contract test will still pass. No auth added. `sm-relay` and the web-remote relay are untouched.
